markdown_report:
**Recommendation:** retain the recent-terminal/Cloze BERT4Rec objective and test one change: replace a small fraction of uniform negatives with moderately hard candidates scored by the same network. No improvement is established yet.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Recent terminal prefixes emphasize contemporary choices and match appended-mask inference. They directly target revival of older isolated interests, although recent purchases do not establish continuing demand. (2) Separately normalized terminal and Cloze losses preserve both next-choice supervision and bidirectional context learning. Their weighting should remain fixed while testing sampling. (3) Electronics has the weakest observed separation: 6.62% negative-beats-positive and a 0.7269 tenth-percentile margin. These single-negative training measurements motivate discrimination experiments but cannot establish validation HR@10.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Hard-BPR highlights false-negative risks in hard sampling [1]. This favors moderate difficulty and a substantial uniform component, rather than selecting only the highest scores. (2) TiSASRec provides machinery for modeling interaction intervals [2]. Adapting temporal biases inside BERT4Rec could address stale interests, but requires additional timestamp plumbing. (3) Recformer motivates finer textual representations [3]. Titles may distinguish direct connections from broad resemblance, but cannot establish compatibility or ownership.

The resulting framework has three directions:

| Direction | Mechanism | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| Target relevance | Recent terminal targets | Recency versus enduring interests |
| Candidate discrimination | Moderate model-scored negatives | Unobserved positives |
| Context specificity | Temporal bias or joint text features | Added complexity and missing attributes |

Three candidate ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell gives a positive reason and a limitation.

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Moderate-negative replacement** | 4: focused combination; established sampling | 7: reusable; benchmark dependent | 7: trains competition; intent unobserved | 8: targets errors; proxy only | 3: sampler change; filtering care |
| Bucketed temporal attention bias | 5: family adaptation; known mechanism | 7: flexible timing; timestamp dependent | 7: addresses stale context; misses compatibility | 5: contextual separation; indirect evidence | 6: compact parameters; interface changes |
| Joint title-token fusion | 5: task adaptation; established fusion | 7: fine detail; sparse text | 7: specific cues; ownership unavailable | 6: richer features; margins may not improve | 7: one network; substantial plumbing |

Select **moderate-negative replacement** at 10% research progress. Retained recent-terminal supervision addresses older-interest revival; harder candidate competition targets broadly plausible items outranking direct recent-interest matches. These are hypotheses, not verified behavioral corrections. The model-facing target is sampled ranking errors, especially Electronics.

For each supervised MASK, draw 128 unique eligible negatives, score without gradients, randomly retain 48, and select 16 from ranks 33–80 among the remainder, ordered by descending score. Optimize positive-versus-64 candidate cross-entropy. Keep all other settings fixed and compare with uniform-64 sampling. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10; retain one checkpoint per category.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276; [2] https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf; [3] https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/kdd23b.pdf.

idea.description: Test bounded moderate-hard negative replacement within each category’s single BERT4Rec, retaining separately normalized recent-terminal and ordinary Cloze supervision. Replace 16 of 64 uniform training negatives with moderately high-scoring candidates from the current network. This is a proposed controlled experiment, not a measured improvement or an executable replacement for the unavailable corrected baseline.
idea.motivation: The retained recent-terminal component targets revival of older isolated interests; competitive candidate training targets broadly related items outranking direct recent-interest matches. Neither mechanism identifies fulfilled needs, ownership or exact compatibility. Electronics’ 6.62% sampled ranking-error rate and 0.7269 lower-tail margin provide a model-facing reason to test discrimination, while remaining distinct from the host’s validation metric. At early research progress, a sampler change is more feasible than introducing text encoders or temporal attention.
idea.implementation_notes:
Use the supplied corrected BERT4Rec and its existing category routing. If the prior mixed objective has not been implemented, define it identically in both comparison conditions: half the examples are recent terminal prefixes and half retain baseline Cloze construction; average supervised losses separately and combine with equal weights. Sample terminal targets uniformly from the latest min(10,n-1) eligible training-history positions, remove the complete future suffix, replace the target with reserved MASK, and left-pad. Every supervised Cloze target is replaced with MASK; no unchanged-target corruption is allowed.

Compare uniform-64 candidate cross-entropy against the proposed replacement sampler with identical architecture, optimizer, objective mixture and temperature 1.0. Use available eligible corrected measurements where their configurations actually match; do not reinterpret the supplied 0.5737 inspiration score as evidence for this proposal. If a comparable uniform control is unavailable, it needs its own budgeted experiment.

For each target, eligible negatives are real catalog IDs excluding PAD, MASK and the user’s complete training-history item set. Use only training histories for this exclusion, never held-out labels. Draw at most 128 uniformly without replacement. If 128 candidates exist, randomly reserve 48, rank the remaining 80 by detached current-model score, and sample 16 without replacement from descending ranks 33 through 80. Thus the highest-scoring 32 remaining candidates are not deliberately selected as hard negatives, although they can occur in the uniform component. Break score ties by item ID. For pools of 65–127 candidates, use 64 uniform candidates; for smaller pools, use all available candidates. Skip targets with no eligible negatives and record counts. This rule bounds mining cost and avoids unbounded rejection sampling; it does not identify false negatives.

Mine with a no-gradient scoring pass using the same model in evaluation mode, then restore its previous mode. Compute the optimization loss with fresh differentiable scores. Chunk supervised positions and preserve exact component loss sums/counts. Candidate cross-entropy is a deliberately sampled classification objective, not an unbiased approximation to full softmax. No importance-correction claim is made.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per completed epoch. Use deterministic separate RNG streams for example construction and negative sampling. Include mining, diagnostics and failures in the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; preallocate comparison compute and report realized updates and elapsed GPU time. Use only pinned validation macro HR@10 for selection; qualitative simulator results and training margins are diagnostic. Maintain the same validation cadence and checkpoint rule across conditions. Each condition trains independent category models for comparison; deploy only the selected condition’s one checkpoint per category, with no averaging or score fusion.

Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and trial-local artifacts. Keep log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), ModelView and the actual nn.Module at view.model. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Diagnostic batches remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), B x L. Keep diagnostic negatives uniformly sampled from a separate fixed stream so changing optimization negatives does not mechanically change the probe. Preserve metric definitions; do not call directional similarity diversity or treat single-negative margins as HR@10.

Inference keeps at most L-1 history items, appends MASK, left-pads and gathers the final nonpadding position using explicit position indices, never count-1. Exclude PAD and MASK from recommendation outputs. Architecture is unchanged, but verify that the predictor writer emits matching configuration and state-dict loading, and that each category loads exactly one checkpoint. Do not fetch weights, inspect other trials or use unavailable reviews, ratings, attributes or simulator traits.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category, initialize the corrected single BERT4Rec with seed 42.
For each completed epoch, execute 200 batches:
    Construct the fixed terminal/Cloze mixture using training histories only.
    Ensure every supervised target is replaced by reserved MASK.
    Compute supervised hidden states through bidirectional BERT4Rec.
    For each supervised target belonging to user u:
        eligible = catalog_ids - {PAD, MASK} - set(training_history[u])
        pool = bounded_uniform_unique_sample(eligible, min(128, len(eligible)))
        if len(pool) == 128:
            uniform = sample_without_replacement(pool, 48)
            remainder = pool minus uniform
            scores = detached_current_model_scores(remainder, dropout_disabled=True)
            ranked = sort_descending(scores, tie_break=item_id)
            moderate = sample_without_replacement(ranked[32:80], 16)
            negatives = concatenate(uniform, moderate)
        else:
            negatives = uniform_unique_sample(pool, min(64, len(pool)))
        if negatives is empty: record and skip target
        logits = differentiable_scores([positive] + negatives)
        accumulate cross_entropy(logits, target_index=0) by objective component
    loss = 0.5 * terminal_mean + 0.5 * cloze_mean
    If only one component is valid, use that component and record the event.
    Update the single network once if any valid targets exist.
Evaluate at the fixed host-compatible cadence.
Compare against otherwise identical uniform-64 training by pinned macro validation HR@10.
Emit one selected checkpoint per category and matching appended-MASK predictor.
Run preserved diagnostics with fixed uniform diagnostic negatives.

originality.positive: Combines inference-aligned recent targets with a precisely bounded moderate-negative replacement rule inside one BERT4Rec.
originality.negative: Hard-negative mixtures and terminal masking are established techniques; this is a focused empirical adaptation.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result can identify whether candidate discrimination merits subsequent temporal or text-aware research.
future_potential.negative: Benefits may depend on sampled evaluation candidates, and false-negative ambiguity remains unresolved.

code_difficulty.positive: Preserves the architecture and predictor, concentrating implementation in sampling and loss construction.
code_difficulty.negative: Unique exclusions, deterministic mining, chunked reduction and model-mode restoration require careful implementation.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Provides the bidirectional masked-item backbone retained throughout the proposal.
Motivates predicting masked items from contextual representations.
limitations: Does not establish gains for the proposed recent-terminal and moderate-negative recipe on the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: Hard-BPR
contributions: The supplied search summary identifies false-negative influence as a concern in dynamic hard sampling.
Motivates retaining random negatives and avoiding exclusive selection of the highest-scoring candidates.
limitations: Its BPR setting differs from masked-target candidate cross-entropy.
The proposed rank window is a heuristic, not a validated false-negative detector.

related_work.title: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Models pairwise interaction intervals alongside positions.
Provides inspiration for an alternative temporal-bias direction within BERT4Rec.
limitations: Its backbone cannot replace the required BERT4Rec family.
Temporal machinery would require compatible inference-time timestamp handling.

related_work.title: Recformer
contributions: Motivates fine-grained textual representations and joint recommendation learning.
Suggests a future direction for distinguishing specific item connections from broad topic similarity.
limitations: Its architecture is not a drop-in replacement for the required backbone.
Text cannot reliably establish ownership, fulfilled demand or exact compatibility.
